title: Counits, transposes and composition under adjoint-equivalence conjugation
statement:
Let $\mathscr C_i,\mathscr N_i$ ($i=1,2,3$) be categories in fixed universes [def-nagata-category]. For each $i$, specify functors $R_i:\mathscr C_i\to\mathscr N_i$, $L_i:\mathscr N_i\to\mathscr C_i$ and an adjunction $R_i\dashv L_i$ whose unit $u_i:1\to L_iR_i$ and counit $e_i:R_iL_i\to1$ are natural isomorphisms satisfying the triangle identities. Use the reverse adjunction $L_i\dashv R_i$ with unit $e_i^{-1}$ and counit $u_i^{-1}$. Composition is written right to left. For any functor $F:\mathscr N_i\to\mathscr N_j$, define $\bar F=L_jFR_i$, and for a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'$ define $\bar\alpha=L_j\alpha R_i$. Define the natural isomorphism
$$c_{F,P}=L_jF(e_{i,P}):\bar F L_iP\longrightarrow L_jFP.$$
For every adjunction $F:\mathscr N_1\rightleftarrows\mathscr N_2:G$ with counit $\epsilon$, form the composite adjunction $\bar F\dashv\bar G$ from $R_1\dashv L_1$, $F\dashv G$, and $L_2\dashv R_2$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Its counit is
$$\bar\epsilon_K=u_{2,K}^{-1}\circ L_2(\epsilon_{R_2K})\circ L_2F(e_{1,GR_2K})\qquad(K\in\mathscr C_2).$$
For $P\in\mathscr N_1$, $N\in\mathscr N_2$ and $a:P\to GN$, the adjoint transpose of $c_{G,N}^{-1}\circ L_1(a):L_1P\to\bar G L_2N$ is
$$L_2(\epsilon_N\circ F(a))\circ c_{F,P}:\bar F L_1P\longrightarrow L_2N.$$
The identifications $c_F,c_G$ are natural in all object maps and in transformations of the functors. For arbitrary $F:\mathscr N_1\to\mathscr N_2$ and $H:\mathscr N_2\to\mathscr N_3$, the maps
$$\kappa_{H,F,K}=L_3H(e_{2,FR_1K}):\bar H\bar F K\longrightarrow\overline{HF}K$$
form a natural isomorphism. For $\alpha:F\to F'$ and $\beta:H\to H'$, writing $*$ for horizontal composition of natural transformations, one has
$$\overline{\beta*\alpha}\circ\kappa_{H,F}=\kappa_{H',F'}\circ(\bar\beta*\bar\alpha).$$
No additive, derived, sheaf-theoretic or nonemptiness hypothesis on these categories is needed.

proof.text: Fix the right-to-left composition convention of the statement. For any adjunction $A\dashv B$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, its Hom bijection sends $s:AX\to Y$ to $B(s)\circ\eta_X$, and its inverse sends $t:X\to BY$ to $\varepsilon_Y\circ A(t)$. These formulas follow directly from the unit/counit description: naturality and the triangles give $B(\varepsilon_Y)\circ BA(t)\circ\eta_X=B(\varepsilon_Y)\circ\eta_{BY}\circ t=t$ and $\varepsilon_Y\circ AB(s)\circ A(\eta_X)=s\circ\varepsilon_{AX}\circ A(\eta_X)=s$. All subsequent reassociations use the category laws of [def-nagata-category].

proof.text: The original triangles and invertibility give $L_i(e_{i,P})=u_{i,L_iP}^{-1}$ and $R_i(u_{i,K})=e_{i,R_iK}^{-1}$. Consequently $u_{i,L_iP}^{-1}\circ L_i(e_{i,P}^{-1})=1$ and $R_i(u_{i,K}^{-1})\circ e_{i,R_iK}^{-1}=1$. These are exactly the two triangles for unit $e_i^{-1}$ and counit $u_i^{-1}$, whose naturality follows by inverting the given naturality equations. Thus they specify the reverse adjunction used in the statement.

proof.text: Compose $R_1\dashv L_1$ with $F\dashv G$ and then $L_2\dashv R_2$, using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The first composition has counit $\epsilon_Q\circ F(e_{1,GQ})$. The second therefore has counit $u_{2,K}^{-1}\circ L_2(\epsilon_{R_2K}\circ F(e_{1,GR_2K}))$. Functoriality of $L_2$ gives exactly the displayed formula for $\bar\epsilon_K$, and the left and right functors are $L_2FR_1$ and $L_1GR_2$.

proof.text: The inverse of $c_{F,P}=L_jF(e_{i,P})$ is $L_jF(e_{i,P}^{-1})$, since functors preserve the two inverse equations. For $q:P\to Q$, naturality of $e_i$ gives $L_jF(q)\circ c_{F,P}=c_{F,Q}\circ\bar F(L_i(q))$. For $\delta:F\to F^{\prime}$, naturality of $\delta$ at $e_{i,P}$ gives $L_j(\delta_P)\circ c_{F,P}=c_{F^{\prime},P}\circ\bar\delta_{L_iP}$. These equations also apply to $G$ and to inverse comparisons, proving all the stated object-map and functor-transformation naturality of $c_F,c_G$.

proof.text: Put $Q=R_2L_2N$ and $b=c_{G,N}^{-1}\circ L_1(a)=L_1(G(e_{2,N}^{-1})\circ a)$. By the composite Hom-bijection clause of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], transpose $b$ successively across $R_1\dashv L_1$, $F\dashv G$, and $L_2\dashv R_2$. The first inverse bijection sends it to $e_{1,GQ}\circ R_1(b)=G(e_{2,N}^{-1})\circ a\circ e_{1,P}$, by naturality of $e_1$. The second sends this to $\epsilon_Q\circ FG(e_{2,N}^{-1})\circ F(a)\circ F(e_{1,P})=e_{2,N}^{-1}\circ\epsilon_N\circ F(a)\circ F(e_{1,P})$, by naturality of $\epsilon$ at $e_{2,N}^{-1}:N\to Q$.

proof.text: Write $t=\epsilon_N\circ F(a)$. The third inverse Hom bijection sends the last map of Step 5 to $u_{2,L_2N}^{-1}\circ L_2(e_{2,N}^{-1})\circ L_2(t)\circ L_2F(e_{1,P})$. The triangle identity from Step 2, $u_{2,L_2N}^{-1}=L_2(e_{2,N})$, cancels its first two factors. The result is $L_2(t)\circ c_{F,P}$, precisely the asserted transpose. This proves the formula for the specified composite adjunction, with no replacement by an unspecified adjunction on the same functors.

proof.text: For arbitrary $F,H$, define $\kappa_K=L_3H(e_{2,FR_1K})$ as in the statement. Its inverse is $L_3H(e_{2,FR_1K}^{-1})$. If $k:K\to K^{\prime}$, the naturality equation $FR_1(k)\circ e_{2,FR_1K}=e_{2,FR_1K^{\prime}}\circ R_2L_2FR_1(k)$, after applying $L_3H$, reads $\overline{HF}(k)\circ\kappa_K=\kappa_{K^{\prime}}\circ\bar H\bar F(k)$. Hence $\kappa$ is a natural isomorphism.

proof.text:
For the transformation square fix $K$ and put $Q=R_1K$, $T=FQ$, $T^{\prime}=F^{\prime}Q$, $x=\alpha_Q:T\to T^{\prime}$. Horizontal composition means $(\beta*\alpha)_Q=\beta_{T^{\prime}}\circ H(x)$. Naturality first of $e_2$ at $x$ and then of $\beta$ at $e_{2,T^{\prime}}$ gives the explicit equality
$$\beta_{T^{\prime}}\circ H(x)\circ H(e_{2,T})=\beta_{T^{\prime}}\circ H(e_{2,T^{\prime}})\circ H(R_2L_2(x))=H^{\prime}(e_{2,T^{\prime}})\circ\beta_{R_2L_2T^{\prime}}\circ H(R_2L_2(x)).$$
Apply $L_3$. The left side is $(\overline{\beta*\alpha})_K\circ\kappa_{H,F,K}$; the right side is $\kappa_{H^{\prime},F^{\prime},K}\circ(\bar\beta*\bar\alpha)_K$. This proves the claimed equality componentwise. Every step used only the specified functors, natural transformations, inverses and triangles, so no additive structure, size beyond the fixed universes, or nonemptiness is required.
